name: 2.1 Stem-and-Leaf Graphs (Stemplots), Line Graphs, and Bar Graphs
_note: Complete on disk, not pushed. 2.1's eleven source problems are all 'construct a graph', which MyOpenMath cannot grade, so every question draws the display itself and asks about it. Slots 2, 6 and 8 are the mistake-variant questions: four versions of one display, three committing an error students actually make, rotated so the answer is not always in the same place. raSHio has no stem-and-leaf, line-graph or bar-graph tool, so this section does not send students there; 2.2 onward will. Points are not split here -- 100 across 14 questions is decided at push time.

questions.title: Read a Stem-and-Leaf Plot - Recover the count in one stem row, the largest value in another, and the total sample size from a stemplot built from randomized data

Choose the Honest Bar Graph - Pick the one bar graph that displays a randomized category table fairly from four versions, three of which commit a classic display error, then name the error in a specified version

Build a Stem-and-Leaf Plot from Raw Data - From an ordered list of two-digit measurements, work out how many stem rows the plot needs, how many leaves land on one stem, and how many values clear a cutoff, then say what a single leaf stands for

Rounding Before a Stemplot - Three-digit prices are rounded to the nearest ten so the hundreds digit can serve as the stem, then read back: round one price, name its leaf, count the prices on one stem, and say why the rounding step is needed

Outliers and Empty Rows in a Stemplot - One value sits far above a tight cluster; read the outlier off the plot, count the stem rows with no leaves, compute the range, and say why the empty rows must still be drawn

Choose the Correct Stem-and-Leaf Plot - Four stemplots of one data set; three commit a classic construction error (repeats written once, leaves out of order, whole values as leaves) and one is right. Pick the correct plot, then name one plot's error
Read a Line Graph Built from a Frequency Table - Recover the sample size, a relative frequency and the most common value from a line graph, then say what the connecting segments do and do not mean

Choose the Correct Line Graph - Four line graphs of one frequency table; three commit a classic error (running totals plotted as frequencies, an axis not starting at zero, frequencies on the wrong values) and one is right

Bar Graph of Counts Versus Percentages - The same table drawn twice, as counts and as percentages; recover the group size, compute one percentage, and say why switching to percentages leaves the shape alone

Over-representation in a Two-Series Bar Graph - A grouped bar graph puts each group's share of an event beside its share of the population; find the over-represented group, measure the gap in percentage points, and say what the graph cannot tell you

Find the Wrong Percentage in a Category Table - A published table gives counts beside percentages, but one percentage does not match its count; find the row, compute what it should be, and state what the column must total
Read a Bar Graph and Compare Categories - Take one count off a drawn bar graph, work out how many more one category holds than another, total the graph, and say why the bars are drawn with gaps

What Each Display Keeps and Throws Away - Decide which display still holds every original value, which suits a categorical variable and which shows change over time, then say what a stemplot gives up as the data grows

Read a Time Series Line Graph - From eight months of data, read one month's value, find the largest month-to-month rise, work out the net change, and say why a line graph suits data collected over time
